subject.title: fix(matrix): tolerate SAS accept events missing method

question: Should OpenClaw accept a Matrix plugin wrapper around matrix-js-sdk's private cryptoBackend.preprocessToDeviceMessages hook for this SAS compatibility case once live proof is provided?
rationale: The code path is the narrow place that sees the malformed to-device event before Rust crypto rejects it, but it depends on a private dependency field in an E2EE trust flow.

options.title: Require proof, then accept the narrow hook
options.body: Require redacted live Matrix verification proof from this branch, then merge if the proof matches the linked failure and maintainers accept the dependency recheck cost.

options.title: Accept with proof override
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly override live proof if they have equivalent private or manual verification and are comfortable owning the private SDK hook.

options.title: Pause for upstream direction
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want the compatibility fix to land in matrix-js-sdk or matrix-rust-sdk instead of OpenClaw's Matrix plugin.

recommendation.title: Require proof, then accept the narrow hook
recommendation.body: Require redacted live Matrix verification proof from this branch, then merge if the proof matches the linked failure and maintainers accept the dependency recheck cost.

likelyOwner.reason: Their Matrix E2EE and verification history is the strongest owner signal for deciding whether this private SDK boundary is acceptable.
